guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Jackson Randy Rhoads model / Gibson Les Paul (Wylde "Bullseye")
guitar.evidence: Randy Rhoads played Gibson Les Pauls and the Karl Sandoval-built polka-dot V (later Jackson's signature Randy Rhoads model) on "Crazy Train"/"Mr. Crowley"; Zakk Wylde's bullseye Gibson Les Paul is iconic for "Bark at the Moon"-era and beyond.
guitar.notes: Was unknown despite Ozzy's guitarists being among the most documented in metal history; filled with high confidence.

tone.target: bright biting Randy Rhodes lead with wah and tight Marshall crunch
tone.profile: bright biting Randy Rhodes lead with wah and tight Marshall crunch
tone.summary: A classic 70s/80s hard rock setup utilizing a Boost for initial grit, followed by a Distortion model (RAT-style) for lead bite, channeled through an AC30 TB to capture the Plexi sound, finished with Wah and Delay effects.

rig.name: Ozzy Osbourne - Crazy Train - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and tighten the overall sound.
Provide initial grit and tighten the attack before distortion.
blocks.gap: The Boost is used to simulate a slight overdriven edge, mimicking early Marshall breakup without heavy fuzz.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the biting, tight lead tone required for Randy Rhoads style solos.
Provide the decisive wah sweeps required for the lead lines.
Simulate the classic Plexi/Marshall sound with bright upper mids.
Provide the classic Marshall-era cabinet tone and punch.
Enhance the upper mids and high frequencies for bite, while controlling low-end mud.
Add subtle echo and perceived sustain to the lead lines.
Add subtle space and dimension without sounding muddy.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for increased upper-mid clarity and punch.

proposals.reason: Enhance the bright, biting upper mids and tight punch required for lead tones.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in solos.
